item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-c2f0421f69157dea","start_unit":4,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"The Supreme Court, by eight votes to three, declared unconstitutional the decree transferring the Guardia Nacional’s administrative and operational control to Sedena, holding that it emptied the constitutional requirement of civil attachment; the ruling also invalidated Sedena’s role in proposing the Guard’s commander. Three judges defended the arrangement as remaining under civilian strategic control.","question_ids":["3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","4B.4","8B.6","8B.8","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"2023; directly concerns the April 2023 institutional conflict and judicial correction of an executive security arrangement.","ruler_attribution":"The decree was enacted by the government led by Andrés Manuel López Obrador; the article identifies the arrangement as part of his administration’s project.","limitations":["The source reports the Court’s legal reasoning and competing judicial views, but does not establish AMLO’s subsequent compliance or implementation beyond the ruling."]},{"source_id":"SRC-3dd25f6c2004fc60","start_unit":1,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"The World Bank reported persistent and recently reversed poverty reduction, worsened education, health-service, and food-security deprivations, especially in southern and rural areas; 2020 national poverty was 43.9%, inequality was 45.4 Gini points, and food inflation disproportionately affected poorer households. Employment recovered by late 2022, but job quality remained weak, with 28% earning one minimum wage or less and 55.8% informal employment.","question_ids":["5B.8","5B.9","5B.10","6B.2","6B.3","6B.6","6B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Published April 2023, using data primarily through 2020 and 2022; relevant as baseline and near-period welfare evidence rather than a complete 2023 outcome assessment.","ruler_attribution":"The brief describes national outcomes during and around AMLO’s administration but does not attribute each indicator causally to him.","limitations":["The document is largely descriptive and does not identify which changes were caused by federal policy, subnational action, or external crises.","Several poverty indicators end in 2020, limiting direct measurement of 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b7c5cd04ebb87c5f","start_unit":3,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"WOLA reported that Sedena acknowledged not recording its detentions in the legally required National Detention Registry, creating apparent substantial under-registration. It also cited Pegasus espionage allegations, concealment of information in Ayotzinapa, continuing torture and excessive-force concerns involving federal forces including the Guardia Nacional, alleged alteration of crime scenes in military executions, inadequate civilian controls, and persistent impunity.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.6","3B.8","3B.9","3B.10","4B.4","4B.9","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","8B.5","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"September 2023 report on conditions and alleged institutional practices during AMLO’s administration.","ruler_attribution":"WOLA attributes the described federal security and transparency context to the Mexican government during AMLO’s presidency; it also reports that AMLO and cabinet members shifted blame for impunity toward the judiciary.","limitations":["WOLA is an advocacy and research organization; the report’s allegations are presented as findings and recommendations but are not independently adjudicated within the supplied text.","The source does not establish AMLO’s personal knowledge of each alleged abuse."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a08bbb6565fd29d9","start_unit":2,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"The Supreme Court invalidated the transfer of Guardia Nacional control to Sedena after opposition senators challenged the reform. The Court majority held that public-security functions must remain civilian and that military assistance must be extraordinary, regulated, supervised, subordinate, and complementary; AMLO reportedly called the ruling a serious error.","question_ids":["3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","4B.4","8B.6","8B.8","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"April 2023; directly records the judicial ruling and the executive reaction.","ruler_attribution":"The challenged reform was approved during AMLO’s administration; the source reports his criticism of the ruling.","limitations":["This source overlaps materially with SRC-c2f0421f69157dea and is retained for its distinct account of the constitutional standards and AMLO’s reaction.","The supplied units do not report whether the administration promptly implemented the ruling."]},{"source_id":"SRC-5cac72c9b3c8a74c","start_unit":2,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"Article 19 reported 696 attacks against the press in 2022, including 12 journalist killings and nine attempted killings, amid increasing stigmatization. It recorded 176 stigmatizing comments in monitored presidential-conference discourse, including 33 attacks directly made by the president, and alleged state omission in preventing attacks, military Pegasus surveillance of journalists and an activist, and impunity linked to criminal-authority collusion.","question_ids":["3B.3","3B.8","3B.9","3B.10","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.1","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","7B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Published March 2023, reporting primarily on 2022 and the first four years of AMLO’s administration.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes repeated stigmatizing presidential discourse to AMLO and describes federal omission and military surveillance during his administration.","limitations":["The attack figures concern 2022, not exclusively 2023.","The source reports Article 19’s assessment and does not establish that AMLO personally ordered surveillance or was personally responsible for each attack."]},{"source_id":"SRC-36bccbc27f88ebff","start_unit":4,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"The GIEI’s sixth report concluded that military, naval, intelligence, police, and other authorities had real-time knowledge of the Ayotzinapa students’ whereabouts, obstructed information, manipulated evidence, and constructed a false account. It reported military presence at locations previously denied, secret operations involving detainees, possible extrajudicial executions, torture-related evidence, and unresolved discrepancies in Sedena records; AMLO had promised to uncover the truth, while his truth commission had classified the case as a state crime.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.6","3B.9","3B.10","4B.4","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","8B.8","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"July 2023 report on a 2014 case and the state’s conduct in the continuing investigation during AMLO’s presidency.","ruler_attribution":"The alleged original abuses and concealment involved state institutions across administrations; AMLO is specifically linked to the promise of investigation and the creation of a truth commission.","limitations":["The GIEI findings concern historical events and investigative conduct, not solely decisions personally made by AMLO in 2023.","The source includes allegations and reported expert conclusions; some possible executions are expressly described as presumptions without identified perpetrators."]},{"source_id":"SRC-5e5814c3b05ad668","start_unit":7,"end_unit":9,"fact_summary":"AMLO denied the GIEI’s findings that military personnel knew of and obstructed the Ayotzinapa investigation, calling them an unfounded campaign to weaken the Army, while asserting that the armed forces were cooperating with justice. The reported GIEI account said soldiers gave false statements and blocked the investigation.","question_ids":["3B.4","7B.1","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","8B.8","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"July 2023; directly records the president’s response to the GIEI’s final report.","ruler_attribution":"The statements and denial are directly attributed to AMLO.","limitations":["The source presents competing claims and does not independently resolve whether AMLO’s denial was accurate or whether cooperation was sufficient."]},{"source_id":"SRC-0f308652ba577d11","start_unit":2,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"A report alleged that AMLO’s son Andrés López Beltrán was connected to a network whose friends benefited from more than 100 million pesos in public contracts, and that he exercised influence over political operations and appointments; the report also described luxury lifestyles and alleged that another son occupied a Houston residence owned by a former Pemex contractor. AMLO defended his sons as private entrepreneurs and denied the reported political succession claim.","question_ids":["4B.5","7B.3","7B.4","7B.5","7B.9","7B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"May 2023; reports allegations and public defenses current to the period.","ruler_attribution":"The allegations concern AMLO’s sons and alleged access to his administration; AMLO is directly attributed with defending them and denying the succession claim.","limitations":["The source presents allegations and journalistic investigations, not final legal or audit findings.","It does not establish that AMLO personally benefited, directed contracts, or knowingly tolerated wrongdoing."]},{"source_id":"SRC-988ebcfe191800db","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"UNICEF reported that Mexican children and adolescents faced substantial welfare deficits: four in ten had overweight or obesity, five in ten experienced violence at home, one in two adolescents experienced physical violence, 70,000 migrant children were detected in 2022, and the pandemic delayed learning by two years. UNICEF described cooperation with Mexican authorities on social protection, nutrition, learning recovery, child-protection systems, violence prevention, legal reform, and migrant-child services.","question_ids":["3B.7","3B.9","6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","6B.5","6B.6","6B.8","6B.9","6B.10","8B.2","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"May 2023 report using mostly 2021–2022 indicators and describing 2022 cooperation with authorities.","ruler_attribution":"The source identifies cooperation with Mexican government authorities but does not assign outcomes or decisions specifically to AMLO.","limitations":["Most indicators predate 2023 and are not causal evaluations of federal policy.","The source describes UNICEF-supported priorities and cooperation, not completed implementation or measured policy effects."]},{"source_id":"SRC-628588bf151aa09d","start_unit":2,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"The GIEI’s sixth and final report said it withdrew from the Ayotzinapa investigation because of state opacity and institutional refusal to provide relevant information. It attributed responsibility for disappearance, murder, evidence manipulation, and concealment to multiple state levels and reported that the students’ whereabouts remained unresolved; AMLO publicly congratulated his government despite these findings.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.9","3B.10","4B.4","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","7B.10","8B.8","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"July 2023; directly covers the final report, withdrawal, unresolved outcome, and presidential response.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes investigative opacity to state institutions during the continuing process and directly reports AMLO’s self-congratulatory response.","limitations":["The publication is a secondary presentation of the GIEI report and has an activist editorial orientation.","The underlying abuses occurred in 2014, while the source addresses later investigative conduct and accountability."]},{"source_id":"SRC-fc634aa51b63f3e5","start_unit":4,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"Mexicans Against Corruption and Impunity reported that the AMLO government failed minimum transparency and open-data standards: 71% of 12,570 government databases had not been updated in at least 24 months, institutional transparency reports fell 36% from 2018 to 2022, and the average institutional score was 29.75/100 with no institutional group passing. It also reported a 24% real budget reduction for INAI from 2018 to 2023 and obstruction of commissioner appointments, impairing the institute’s operation.","question_ids":["4B.4","4B.6","4B.9","5B.5","5B.7","7B.1","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","7B.10","8B.5","8B.6","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"August 2023 report evaluating transparency performance through 2022 and institutional conditions in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report directly evaluates the government of López Obrador and attributes the reduced transparency, budget reduction, and blocked appointments to his administration.","limitations":["The source is produced by an anti-corruption investigative organization and presents its own methodology and interpretation.","The supplied text does not distinguish every decision made personally by AMLO from those made by agencies or the legislature."]},{"source_id":"SRC-add77bbe4e69c6b9","start_unit":1,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"The Reuters Institute reported daily verbal attacks by AMLO against news organizations and journalists, including prominent named targets; 180 journalists had demanded an end to harassment, three journalists were murdered in the first three months of 2023, and Article 19 alleged government disinformation and curtailed legal access to public information. It also reported a 26.5% estimate that public information supplied by authorities was false, alongside continuing media competition and audience growth for some outlets.","question_ids":["3B.3","3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.1","7B.2","7B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"June 2023 country report, with 2023 killings and recent trends.","ruler_attribution":"Daily attacks are directly attributed to AMLO; allegations concerning disinformation and access to information are attributed to Article 19.","limitations":["The 26.5% false-information figure is an Article 19 claim reported by the Reuters Institute, not independently validated in the supplied text.","The source notes media resilience and audience growth but does not evaluate government support for those developments."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":[],"batch_limitations":["The supplied corpus contains substantial evidence on civil-military control, human rights, press freedom, transparency, integrity allegations, poverty, and child welfare, but little or no direct evidence on nuclear risk, arms control, international war decisions, macroeconomic rules, or some effectiveness dimensions.","Facts are reported as source findings or allegations where the documents do not establish adjudicated responsibility or causal attribution to AMLO personally.","Several sources describe outcomes from 2020–2022 or historical events before 2023; their relevance to the 2023 ruler-period is therefore qualified by timing and attribution limits."]}
